naming_rules: Node grammar: value:<entity>.<quantity>[<Qualifier>] with entity in {player, enemy, unit, spawner, island, item, weapon, armor, amulet, rage, ability, reward, economy, sim, forecast, ads, time}; state:<name> for exogenous runtime input; config:<Class>.<field path> exactly as in data_dictionary.csv. Use ONLY the value:/state: nodes in this vocabulary (copy them character for character, brackets included). Do not invent new ones. If nothing fits, use the closest generic node and say so in the note. QUALIFIERS: a qualified node value:x.q[Q] is a specialisation of the generic value:x.q, and the graph builder adds the edge generic->qualified. A formula that works over every StatType or meta key (stats.raw_value_aggregation, stats.specific_value_pipeline, stats.specific_cap, stats.specific_identity, meta.metastat_value) outputs the generic node plus the qualified nodes listed with it as producer. A formula specific to one stat reads or writes the qualified node. Player/enemy stat qualifiers are only the listed StatType names. Typed damage and defence stats are never qualified per type (no [StabDamageFlat]). Use the group qualifiers [DamageFlatByType], [DamagePercentByType], [DefenceFlatByType] and [DefencePercentByType], meaning the stat that the weapon or hit damage type selects. Keep player and enemy apart. Read player.* for the player's stats and enemy.* for a spawned enemy's stats (an enemy's Health is value:enemy.stat_raw[Health]). value:unit.* is only for the few nodes that truly apply to either side. STAT CHAIN: modifier producers write their own node (item.equip_stat_modifiers, ability.stat_modifier, player.upgrade_stat_modifier, rage.extra_health_modifier, reward.granted_stat_modifier, player.event_percent_factor). stats.modifier_merge, stats.temporary_modifier_decay and powerups.amulet_stat_apply read them and write player.stat_modifiers (enemy.stat_modifiers for enemies). stats.raw_value_aggregation reads config:PlayerConfig.Stats[...] (or player.stat_base) plus player.stat_modifiers and writes player.stat_raw[...]. For enemies it reads enemy.stat_base plus enemy.stat_modifiers. The curves and the specific pipeline read stat_raw[X] and write stat_specific[X]. Meta stats: value:player.meta_stat[<MetaStatsConfig key>] for the listed keys and value:player.meta_stat for the rest. Upgrade levers flow through player.upgrade_level -> player.upgrade_meta_modifier -> meta.metastat_value. stat_drop at a spawner's island is value:spawner.stat_drop_multiplier (there is no meta_stat[stat_drop]). REWARD CHAIN: enemy.stat_rewards x spawner.stat_drop_multiplier x spawner.kill_reward_multiplier produce reward.devour_stat_modifier. meta.devour_stat_grant (which also reads ability.double_loot_multiplier, state:vip_level, state:cheats and state:rng) turns it into reward.granted_stat_modifier, which then enters stats.modifier_merge. Quest, shop, ads and baked rewards also end in reward.granted_stat_modifier, through reward.quest_stat_reward_scaled, reward.baked_stat_reward and ads.rewarded_stat_value. Item copies use reward.item_copies_per_kill and reward.item_copies_granted -> items.copy_merge -> item.copies -> item.effective_level -> weapon.item_damage / armor.item_armor. weapon.item_damage feeds player.outgoing_damage_per_hit and sim.dps_by_damage_type. SPAWNER ECONOMY: spawner.charges_total, spawner.charges_limit_per_day and spawner.small_cooldown feed sim.stat_rpm, sim.soul_rpm and spawner.daily_*. Every RPM/GPM consumer (ads, baked rewards, crystal mob bonus, dynamic weights, snapshot gpm) reads value:sim.stat_rpm. SIMULATION / BAKE: data stored in the SimulationData asset is generated by the original simulation. Always reference it as value:sim.snapshot_stat_value, sim.snapshot_stat_total, sim.snapshot_stat_gpm, sim.dps_by_damage_type, sim.defense_by_damage_type and sim.snapshot_progress, never as config:SimulationData.*. Snapshot lookups read those nodes and write value:sim.snapshot_at_time. Bake and forecast formulas read sim.snapshot_at_time, and they recompute crit, block and dodge inline from it rather than reading live player nodes. Bake formulas output both value:sim.bake_new_health or sim.bake_new_damage and config:EnemySpawnerConfig.Stats[Health] or [Damage]. Editor generators output config: nodes only (role config). Interpolation: x = value:sim.balance_timing (or time.island_timing_days for island-based conversions) -> sim.balance_coefficient[<BalanceInterpolationType>]. FORECAST: sim.snapshot_at_time -> forecast.snapshot -> forecast.enemy_health/enemy_damage/stat_reward -> forecast.event_plan. From the plan, spawners.event_plan_override writes enemy.override_base_stats, enemy.damage_type, enemy.resist_by_damage_type and enemy.stat_rewards. enemy.override_base_stats then goes through spawners.enemy_spawn_stats (with enemy.ab_hp_damage_multiplier) to enemy.stat_base. LOOKUP TABLES: lookup_table formulas output their own value node, but other formulas should read the authored config: node directly when they consume the raw table. HP: every change to current HP writes player.current_hp or enemy.current_hp. Per-hit damage nodes are player.outgoing_damage_per_hit (player hits enemy) and player.incoming_damage_per_hit (enemy hits player). STATE: use state: only for inputs that no catalogued formula computes (dt, rng, clock, input, positions, player actions, ads/IAP events, VIP level, AB cohort, active event, boss-tower context, quest progress, crystals, cheats, raw save counters, sim bot internals). Hard-coded numbers are constant:<CodeFileStem>.<name>.
